1.explanation: This minimal example mounts a ComposedModal via a React portal at the top level. We pass size="lg" to show the padding behavior, and hasForm on ModalBody to remove the default content padding for form controls. Inside we render a single TextInput. When you run this component and open the modal, you should see the input span the full width of the modal (edge-to-edge). Due to the regression, however, it remains inset by 20%, reproducing the bug shown in your screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: In the ComposedModal example below, the TextInput field does not span the full width of the modal body as expected. Instead it is inset by the default 20% padding on the right even though the body has a form. According to the spec, when you pass hasForm to ModalBody, any form controls inside should edge-to-edge without that extra padding.
